title: Use of AI‑driven ultrasound systems to improve diagnostic accuracy in prenatal medicine - ADINOPRE study
summary: This study investigates whether AI-assisted ultrasound devices can improve the quality of pregnancy ultrasounds. Each participant receives two ultrasound examinations in succession during a single appointment—one performed by a physician with standard training and one by an experienced expert. AI support is also used during the examinations to automatically assist in identifying the correct image planes and taking measurements. The aim is to find out whether AI can help reduce examination errors and shorten examination times.

interventions.name: Arm 1 – Sequence: Manual → AI-assisted; ultrasound examination by a standard examiner (scan A: manual, then AI-assisted) and by an expert examiner (scan B: manual, then AI-assisted). Independent image evaluation by a DEGUM II/III expert. Patient satisfaction survey and self-assessment by the examine

Arm 2 – Sequence: AI-supported → Manual; Ultrasound examination by a standard examiner (scan A: AI-assisted, followed by manual) and by an expert examiner (scan B: AI-assisted, followed by manual). Independent image evaluation by a DEGUM II/III expert. Patient satisfaction survey and self-assessment

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-	Singleton pregnancy
-	Gestational age 19+0 – 23+6 weeks (crown–rump length or reliable dating)
-	Written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
-	Multiple pregnancy
-	Intra uterine fetal demise
-	Maternal condition precluding adequate scan (e.g. critical illness, abdominal wall infection) Inability to give consent (language barrier, cognitive impairment)
